title: Single audit planning — Riverbend County
instructions: Riverbend County's fiscal year began July 1, 2025. Using the federal expenditure data, determine whether a single audit is required and plan major program coverage. Riverbend does **not** qualify as a low-risk auditee.

exhibits.title: Schedule of expenditures of federal awards
exhibits.content:
| Program | Expenditures |
|---|---:|
| Highway Planning and Construction | 6,000,000 |
| Child Nutrition Cluster | 2,500,000 |
| Head Start | 900,000 |
| Community Development Block Grants | 400,000 |
| Emergency Food Assistance | 200,000 |

exhibits.title: Guidance
exhibits.content:
- Single audit threshold: **$1,000,000** of federal expenditures.
- Type A threshold for this auditee: **$1,000,000**.
- Major programs must cover at least **40%** of total federal expenditures (**20%** for a low-risk auditee).

rows.label: Is a single audit required?
options: No — a program-specific audit is required instead
No — federal expenditures are below the threshold
rows.explanation: Expenditures of 10,000,000 exceed the 1,000,000 threshold, and the county has several programs, so a **single audit** is required.

rows.label: Which additional report does the single audit require?
options: An opinion on compliance for each major program
An opinion on the effectiveness of internal control over all programs
A review report on the schedule of expenditures
rows.answer: An opinion on compliance for each major program
rows.explanation: The auditor opines on compliance for each major program, reports on internal control over compliance, and gives an in-relation-to opinion on the schedule of expenditures.
